chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Jelly Roll lecturing day people and believing in yourself
summary: Danny describes Jelly Roll holding forth to newcomers on the corner with his diamond, and says you had to believe in yourself to survive in New York.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah, anyway each town had these people with these names, and they were Night People. And they'd talk different from day people. Now, Jelly Roll would stand on the corner, like I mentioned before, and talk to a bunch of day people, a bunch of cats who'd come off the plantation in Trinidad or something, and they'd come to New York and you'd see them with their little hats they had on, and other cats out of Georgia -- people that had nothing to do with show business. But they'd come around because of the excitement around musicians and show... And they'd stand up there, and Jelly Roll was lecturing them. See, half of them don't know what Jelly's talking about.

And Jelly's signifying, saying "Yeah, I did this and I did that." And he opens his mouth, and he's got that diamond in his tooth, and they're looking at that: "Watch when he's opening his mouth? You can see his diamond." They should have asked permission or paid, said, "Let me see your diamond" or did one of them things. But they had never seen no man stand on a corner like that, talking with his sleeves rolled up, with them nice, pretty shirts on and good clothes. Of course, he was a little dated, you know. But he was class.
Yeah. He had a new car.

Yeah. And he believed in himself. And that's what it took in them days. You had to believe in yourself. Just like me to survive in New York. I didn't say nothing, but I used to say to myself, 'Goddamn, they ain't gonna to starve me, hell or high water.' That's the attitude you had. If you didn't...
